title: Mekhi and the Dawgs: Four Seasons, One Name, Still Hunting the First Bowl
body: Some managers rebrand every fall. Mekhi has run the Dawgs since day one of the Buckaroo Football League, and the loyalty is admirable even if the trophy case is still empty. He arrived in 2023 with what might be the deepest football knowledge in the league and went 6-8 with 1,542.8 points. That was good enough for the 4 seed and a 4th-place finish out of six, a respectable debut for a franchise that looked ready to climb.

Instead, 2024 went sideways. The Dawgs slipped to 5-9, scored 1,413.5 points, and finished 5th as the 5 seed. The low point came in week 14, when Mekhi put up a career-worst 67.9 against Randy, the kind of number that makes a football mind stare at the ceiling. He did not make a single trade in either of his first two seasons, preferring to work the waiver wire: 9 pickups in 2023 and 6 in 2024.

2025 was the strangest season in Dawgs history. Mekhi drafted from basic training, which is not the ideal setting for scouting sleepers, and then built the best offense he has ever had: 1,858.2 points, an 8-8 record, the 4 seed, and a career-best 153.6 against Randy in week 9. The payoff never came. The consolation ladder dropped the Dawgs to 6th of 6, and Mekhi's name went on the last-place line right below Sonny's two years of Ben Dover. His all-time playoff record sits at 0-1, a reminder that in this league January is not guaranteed to reward a good October.

The head-to-head ledger tells the rest of the story. Kaushal is the clear nemesis at 9-2 against the Dawgs, and those two Habibsters titles did not come without a few Dawgs casualties along the way. Mekhi trails Sonny 5-7, Alan 4-6 and Ramon 3-6, but the Randy rivalry is dead even at 6-6. Both his best and worst weeks came against The fumblers, so it may be the most unpredictable matchup in the league. He is also a perfect 1-0 against both newcomers, Jordan and Zoe, a warm welcome to the expanded league.

Now in 2026, Kai drafted from overseas, extending one of the league's unluckiest traditions, and the Dawgs sit at 2-5 with 736 points and 1% title odds. True to form, he has not stopped grinding: 8 pickups through seven weeks, already matching last year's total, plus his second career trade. The waiver-wire king is still working every angle. The season looks bleak on paper, but Mekhi has shown he can score with anyone, and the first Dawgs title would make a great story whenever it comes.
